subject: Money
title: Tulip Mania
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Tulip Mania.

hook.text: In 1637, a single tulip bulb sold for 10,000 guilders—enough to buy a canal house in Amsterdam.

buildup.text: Tulips arrived in Holland in the 1590s. Rare striped varieties became status symbols among the wealthy.

discovery.text: Speculators began trading tulip futures. People who'd never seen a tulip traded contracts on bulbs still in the ground.

twist.text: In February 1637, buyers stopped showing up at auction. Prices crashed 99% in days. Fortunes vanished overnight.

climax.text: Modern historians debate how widespread the mania was. But the story endures as the archetype of all bubbles.

punchline.text: A flower worth a fortune. Until it wasn't.

quiz.question: What made tulip mania the archetype of financial bubbles?
options: Tulips were the most expensive commodity
Prices skyrocketed on speculation then crashed 99%
